chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about breaking the fast before the prayer or after it, so he said: 'If he is with a group of people and fears that he will detain them from their evening meal, let him break the fast with them; and if it is otherwise, let him pray and then break the fast.'

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: The prayer (specifically Maghrib in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred order of breaking the fast and performing Maghrib prayer when dining with others?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* highlights the juristic principle of *al-maslahah al-mursalah* (public interest) and *ihsan* (social grace) in balancing ritual precision with communal harmony. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on flexibility in *fiqh*, prioritizing the comfort of the congregation over rigid procedural order when no harm is incurred. The ruling underscores the Prophet’s practical approach to daily worship, integrating social etiquette into the legal framework of fasting.
